name: Nine Orchard
positioning: Hotel in the restored former Jarmulowsky Bank, built in 1912, on the Lower East Side of downtown New York
best_for: Travelers who love historic architecture and design
Adults wanting a downtown Lower East Side base

facts.text: Nine Orchard occupies the restored and reimagined former Jarmulowsky Bank.
The Jarmulowsky Bank building was originally built in 1912.
The hotel is on the corner of Orchard and Canal Street on the Lower East Side.
Rooms keep original Neo-Renaissance details, including original moldings, with large windows that fill the space with natural light.
Rooms feature commissioned artworks by local artists.
Rooms are labeled like New York apartments, such as 2A or 4F, as an homage to city apartment living.
The Corner King rooms have curved corner windows.
The Design Suite has sweeping Manhattan skyline views and an enhanced minibar with a Subzero fridge.
The first floor has Corner Bar, an all-day restaurant inspired by classic taverns, and the Swan Room, a living room by day and cocktail lounge by night.
The A, C and F trains are a one-minute walk from the hotel.
The hotel has three event spaces for gatherings small and large.

highlights.text: The Swan Room sits in the former bank teller room, with its vaulted ceiling and pink Tennessee marble walls.
Rooms have custom-made Ojas speakers programmed with New York-inspired stations curated by Devon Turnbull and DJ Stretch Armstrong.
The Terrace Suite has a private terrace and sweeping city skyline views.
The Two Bedroom Terrace Suite has a private terrace with lounge chairs and a dining table.

considerations.text: Conde Nast Traveler notes that the city location comes with street noise, so light sleepers may want earplugs.
Conde Nast Traveler describes the overall vibe as chic, cool and largely for adults.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.
